summary.one_liner: Multiplex is a command-line process multiplexer with a compact syntax for running several processes in parallel, coordinating them with delays and dependencies, and merging their output.
summary.what_it_does: Runs multiple commands in parallel from a single CLI invocation, without a config file, and gracefully shuts down child processes. Its output streams are multiplexed to stdout and stderr in a format that is easy to parse with standard command-line tools. A compact command syntax supports named channels, colors, start delays, dependencies on other processes ending or starting, and actions such as terminating everything when one process ends. Guards let a command wait for a glob or regexp match in a process's output or on standard input. The tool also offers detached, filesystem-backed runs managed with start, status, tail and stop subcommands, and a simple Python API.
use_cases: run a web server, database and worker together
combine output from multiple parallel commands
start a service and run a test once it is ready
sequential build then run pipeline without a shell script
run background processes detached from the terminal
how_to_run: multiplex start dev "API=npm run dev" "WEB=npm run web"
notable: Compact one-line syntax for delays, dependencies, colors and actions, with no config file needed
Dependencies can wait on a process start (&) or end, chained with delays
Guards match glob or regexp patterns in process stdout, stderr or standard input
Detached runs with state and logs stored in .multiplex/ directory
Optional Python API for more advanced orchestration
caveats: Only tested on Linux and macOS according to the README
Input guards consume standard input and only work in foreground mode
Guard names must not collide with action names
